sections.text_helper: Section 9.4.5 "HSIK and PSIK clock" in chapter 9 (Reset and clock control (RCC)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 260.
sections.section_content:
THE HSIK and PSIK are two clock outputs offering frequency flexibility to the user. These
dividers can be configured thanks to HSIKDIV[3:0] and PSIKDIV[3:0] bitfields respectively
with division factors of 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 ... 7.5, and 8. This allow to create a 96 MHz clock
source derived from a 144 MHz for example if divided by 1.5, useful for FDCAN operation,
or 64 MHz out of the 160 MHz divided by 2.5 to tune your DAC output sample frequency.
The HSIKRDY and PSIKRDY flags in the RCC_CR register indicate whether the HSIK and
PSIK clocks are stable or not. At startup, the HSIK, and PSIK output clocks are not released
until this bit is set by hardware.
The HSIK and PSIK clock signals can be switched on and off using the HSIKON and
PSIKON bits in the RCC_CR register.
[Table 67. PSIK and HSIK output frequency]
Caution: 160 MHz is above the maximum frequency supported by the product. It must not be
propagated to the kernel clock of peripherals.
